timeouts._comment: Wall-clock ceiling in minutes, per queue (same q.* keys as concurrency, a confirmed gap this repo had: only retry-attempt-count (retry block below) and dollar-budget (project.json budget.hard_stop_at) limits existed before this. Bounds CUMULATIVE with_retry() loop time across attempts+backoff for operations passed a queue= argument - it does NOT interrupt a single hung call mid-flight (e.g. a subprocess with no timeout of its own); that needs its own timeout at the call site. q.render's 90min sits comfortably above CLAUDE.md section 10's documented legitimate 45-60min range so it catches genuine runaways, not normal-but-slow renders.

fallback._comment: Piper (scripts/piper_client.py) as a local, free, no-network TTS path when ElevenLabs (scripts/elevenlabs_client.py) can't initialize (missing ELEVENLABS_API_KEY) or exhausts quota mid-batch (a confirmed real occurrence three times per production_ledger.py's own docstring). scripts/lib/tts_providers.py's select_tts_provider() only falls back when this is true, and only ever returns Piper with quality_gate='draft_only' attached to every result it produces - law #4 (no silent degradation): a robotic local voice must never quietly become the delivered master. Same fallback_to_still shape as flow_account_pool below, mirrored for the audio provider.

pre_generation_approval._comment: User rule, 2026-08-09: no ElevenLabs generation (scripts/elevenlabs_client.py text_to_speech()/generate_music()) runs without the human seeing the exact character count and estimated cost/credit usage FIRST and explicitly approving - added after this project's narration was generated once already ahead of a duration decision, which the user wants to avoid repeating. This is a human gate (CLAUDE.md law #7), not a script-enforced block - the discipline is: compute+present the count, wait for an explicit yes, THEN call text_to_speech(). A cache hit (ArtifactCache.reuse(), zero new characters) does not need this gate - only genuinely new generation does.
